deities: Goddess Durga as Chakkulathamma (Vana Durga, eight-armed Bhagavathi)
festivals: Pongala (Vrischikam, November-December; the grand annual festival — lakhs of women devotees cook pongala nivedyam in earthen pots; only women participate)
Panthrandu Noyampu (Dhanu month; 12 days of fasting and prayer from the first day of Dhanu till the twelfth)
Naree Pooja (first Friday of December; the male priest washes the feet of women devotees who fasted)

history.period: Ancient (believed over 3000 years; legendary origins); modern prominence from a late-20th-century renovation
history.summary: Chakkulathukavu is one of Kerala's most renowned Bhagavathi (Durga) temples, at Neerattupuram in Thalavady panchayat, on the banks of the holy Pampa river. Local legend says a hunter found the goddess's image — Goddess Vanadurga — inside a chithalputtu (ant-hill shell) after Narada appeared to him in the form of a stranger, and the place grew in sanctity from that incident. The temple claims an antiquity of over 3000 years, but it was little known even to local residents, serving only as a family temple of a local resident until it was renovated a few decades ago, after which it rose to become one of the state's most visited pilgrim centres. The presiding deity is worshipped as Chakkulathamma, an eight-armed idol of Vana Durga, alongside shrines of Ayyappa, Vishnu, Shiva, Murugan, Ganapathi, Yakshi and serpent gods. The temple is open to people of all faiths and is managed by a private family trust.

name: Chakkulathukavu Temple
town_description: Thalavady is a panchayat in the Kuttanad region of Alappuzha district, in the rice-bowl lowlands of central Kerala. Chakkulathukavu stands at Neerattupuram within it, near the border of Alappuzha and Pathanamthitta districts, on the banks of the holy Pampa river with the Manimala river flowing nearby. The area is part of the Kuttanad below-sea-level farming belt, known for its paddy fields, backwater canals and coconut groves.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport (approx. 115-120 km; taxis and pre-paid cabs available); Thiruvananthapuram International Airport is about 150 km.
travel.railway: Thiruvalla Railway Station (approx. 9-12 km), well connected across Kerala and South India.
travel.road: Neerattupuram, on the Thiruvalla–Ambalapuzha road (approx. 18 km from Ambalapuzha). KSRTC buses ply frequently from Thiruvalla to Alappuzha via Chakkulathukavu; Neerattupuram bus stop is the nearest. Autos and taxis run from Thiruvalla and Ambalapuzha.

visitor_information.best_time: September to March for pleasant weather; Pongala (November-December, on Thrikkarthika day) is the most spiritually charged but extremely crowded time — the queue of women devotees stretches up to 20 km. Fridays are considered especially auspicious for the Goddess.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 4:30 AM to 1:00 PM; evening 4:30 PM to 8:00 PM, open all days (verify — one source lists 4:00 AM-11:30 AM / 5:00 PM-8:00 PM, and JustDial lists only 5:00 AM-1:00 PM daily). Entry is free. Men must remove shirts before entering the sanctum; mobile phones and cameras are not allowed inside.
